newsitem.title: GERMANY: Weather spurs German winter sowing, beet harvest.
newsitem.headline: Weather spurs German winter sowing, beet harvest.

text.p: Winter grain plantings and the beet harvest are advancing in Germany, aided by mostly dry weather, the DWD meteorological office said in a weekly report.
Winter rye was mostly finished and winter wheat plantings had started in some regions, while rapeseed and barley were already in their early growth stages, it said.
"Drier weather than in recent weeks helps speed up the sugar beet harvest, but temperatures are too cool for the feed maize crop, which is still being harvested," a DWD source said.
"But cool weather allows the rapeseed crop to develop slowly, which will harden it ahead of frost in the winter."
DWD forecast dry weather and maximum daytime temperatures at around 15 degrees in the week to October 16, having recorded 11-16 degrees in the October 3-9 period.
